name: denial_of_service
description: Unbounded loop over growing user-controlled array causing denial-of-service via block gas limit
question: The source file in `source` contains a function that iterates with a for-loop over a dynamic array (e.g. a state array like `stakers`, `positions`, or `recipients`) that grows via user actions, performing per-element external calls or transfers inside the loop, without any pagination, batch-size limit, or cap on array length, such that as the array grows the function can exceed the block gas limit and become permanently uncallable, causing denial-of-service for fund distribution or other critical operations.
criteria: A for/while loop bounded by `array.length` where the array is a public/state variable appended to by users (e.g. via deposit, stake, register functions)
No pagination parameters (like `startIndex`/`batchSize`) or fixed maximum iteration count limiting the loop
Loop body performs external calls, ETH transfers, or token transfers per iteration (e.g. `_sendReward`, `.transfer`, `.call{value:}`)
No pull-based claim function as an alternative to the push-based loop
Function lacks any check reverting or skipping when array length would make gas cost exceed block limits
